headline: Sellers Swamp the Tape as Financials and Software Lead a Broad Retreat
body_html:
Wall Street sold off across the board on Tuesday. Of the 664 stocks we track, 519 finished lower and just 143 higher. The market's fear gauge has been climbing again, and the unease reaches beyond the artificial-intelligence worries that drove earlier wobbles. Investors appeared to be cutting risk everywhere.

Sector moves showed how lopsided the session was. Semiconductors were the only group in positive territory, up 0.23%. Healthcare, down 0.53%, and materials, down 0.84%, held up best among the decliners. Financials took the heaviest damage, falling 5.15%, and software gave back 2.88%. Homebuilders fell 1.91% after a survey showed builder sentiment at its lowest in more than fourteen years.

The standout mover ran against the tide. AECOM jumped 11.12%, the best showing in our universe. On the other side, Nextracker dropped 12.13% and Salesforce lost 9.41%. When this many stocks fall together and only a few pockets of strength survive, the market is usually trading on mood rather than individual stories. The test on Wednesday, November 18 is whether buyers step in, or whether the chip sector's narrow lead gives way as well.

briefs.headline: Financials Suffer the Session's Deepest Cut
briefs.body: The financial sector fell 5.15%, the steepest drop of any group we follow and well ahead of the next-worst. With most of the market already under pressure, the scale of the slide made it the clearest sign of risk reduction on Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Software Names Sell Off Hard
briefs.body: The software group lost 2.88%, with Salesforce sliding 9.41% and BlackBerry falling 7.01%. The pullback fits a wider theme of money leaving technology for more defensive corners of the market.

briefs.headline: Solar Equipment Makers Hit the Skids
briefs.body: Nextracker was the session's worst performer, down 12.13%, and Enphase Energy fell 7.58%. Together the two losses made solar one of the weakest pockets of an already weak tape, with no sign of a bounce into the close.

briefs.headline: Builder Gloom Weighs on Homebuilders
briefs.body: Homebuilders slipped 1.91% after a sentiment survey sank to its lowest reading in more than fourteen years. Reports also said more builders are cutting prices to move inventory, a sign that demand remains soft.

briefs.headline: Gulf Tensions Keep Energy Under a Cloud
briefs.body: Reports of a gas tanker abandoned off Oman after a projectile strike, and of Houthi drones aimed toward a Saudi pipeline, kept the Middle East in view. Even so, energy shares fell 1.49% on the day, as the broad selloff overshadowed the geopolitical risk.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Hold Their Ground
briefs.body: Semiconductors were the lone gaining sector, up 0.23%. Arm Holdings rose 4.76% and Astera Labs added 4.58%. The gains were modest, but they stood out in a session where almost everything else fell, ahead of a closely watched chip-sector earnings report.
